'''Endel Lippmaa''' (15 September 1930 – 30 July 2015)<ref name="delfi">[http://www.delfi.ee/news/paevauudised/eesti/suri-teadlane-ja-poliitik-endel-lippmaa?id=72036127 The Telegraph. ''Endel Lippmaa, physicist - obituary'' 16 August 2015]</ref> was an [[Estonia]]n scientist, academician, politician, and twice government minister in 1990–1991 and 1995–1996.

Lippmaa was founder and chairman of the Science Council of the [[National Institute of Chemical Physics and Biophysics]]. He was also head chairman and professor of chemical physics, physical chemistry, physics, and mathematics at the [[Estonian Academy of Sciences]] and was highly regarded in his work [https://physicstoday.scitation.org/do/10.1063/PT.5.010327/full/ into solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR)]. In 1999, he was voted one of the [[100 great Estonians of the 20th century]].

==Scientific and political career==

In 1972, Endel Lippmaa was elected as a Member of the [[Estonian Academy of Sciences]]. He served as a member of the Board of the Academy for the period 1975–2014. In 1977-1982 he was Secretary-Academician of the Division of Physics, Mathematics and Engineering, in 1999-2004 Head of the Division of Astronomy and Physics, in 2007-2010 Chairman of the Energy Council of the Academy.<ref>[https://physicstoday.scitation.org/do/10.1063/PT.5.6165/full/ "Scientific career"], ''[[Physics Today]]'', England, 4 August 2015.</ref>

During Lippmaa's time working in physics, he wrote a paper on "Structural studies of silicates by solid-state high-resolution silicon-29 NMR,".<ref>[https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja00535a008 Structural studies of silicates by solid-state high-resolution silicon-29 NMR,""], Journal of the American Chemical Society Vol 102 Issue 15 pages 4889 - 4893 (1980)</ref> This paper, now highly regarded, demonstrated in 1980 that high-resolution NMR spectroscopy could be applied profitably to inorganic samples, not just organic or biological ones. According to [[Google Scholar]], the paper has garnered 1496 citations as at May 2025.

During the [[Singing revolution]] he was an active member of the [[Popular Front of Estonia]]. He was in 1989 elected member the new Soviet parliament, the Congress of People's Deputies.<ref>{{cite news |title=This Stupidity Must Stop |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/staten-island-advance-endel-lippmaa-193/169903924/ |work=Staten Island Advance |date=July 2, 1989 |location=Staten Island, NY |page=48 |access-date=April 9, 2025 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Porubcansky |first1=Mark J. |title=Glasnost Has Opened Up Soviet Activists' Eyes ... and What They See Is Pollution |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/staten-island-advance-endel-lippmaa-193/169903888/ |work=Staten Island Advance |date=July 2, 1989 |location=Staten Island, NY |page=48 |access-date=April 9, 2025 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref>  In 1989, in the newly elected Soviet Congress he become best known for his work in uncovering and denouncing of the crucial documents of the 1939 [[Nazi-Soviet Pact]] which in June 1940 had resulted in the [[Stalin|Stalinist]] Soviet Union's military invasion, occupation and illegal annexation of three Baltic countries: Estonia, [[Latvia]] and [[Lithuania]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Soviet Assembly Finds Protocols to 1939 Pact with Nazis Illegal |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-boston-globe-endel-lippmaa-1930-201/169904185/ |work=The Boston Globe |date=December 25, 1989 |location=Boston, MA |page=41 |access-date=April 9, 2025 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/11801251/Endel-Lippmaa-physicist-obituary.html</ref><ref>https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/Online/19158/Endel-Lippmaa</ref>

At the time when Estonia restored full independence from the USSR, in 1990–1991, he was Minister for the Eastern Affairs of the [[Republic of Estonia]] (in the government cabinets led by prime ministers [[Edgar Savisaar]] and [[Tiit Vähi]], respectively). In 1990–1992 he was elected member of the [[Congress of Estonia]]. Later he was a founding member of the [[Estonian Coalition Party|Coalition Party]]. In 1995–1996 he served as Minister of European Affairs, and in 1996-1999 he was elected Member of Parliament (''[[Riigikogu]]'').

==Personal life==
Endel Lippmaa was born in [[Tartu]]. His father was the botanist [[Teodor Lippmaa]], and his maternal grandfather was the writer and journalist [[Jakob Mändmets]]. He graduated from [[Nõmme High School]] in 1948 and from [[Tallinn University of Technology]] (TUT) in 1953, where he majored in oil shale technology.<ref>[https://physicstoday.scitation.org/do/10.1063/PT.5.6165/full/ "In 1948 he graduated from Nõmme Gymnasium and in 1953 Tallinn University of Technology (TUT) majoring in oil shale technology"], ''[[Physics Today]]'', England, 4 August 2015.</ref>

Lippmaa was married to Helle Lippmaa and had two sons, Jaak Lippmaa and Mikk Lippmaa.<ref name="delfi" />

==Awards==
In 2000, Lippmaa was awarded the [[Order of the National Coat of Arms]], II Class.
